_comment: Campaign config for build_report.py. Copy this file, fill in your target's values, and pass it via --config. All target-specific TEXT lives here so the report builder stays target-agnostic. Structure FACTS (resolution, experimental method, deposition date) are NOT set here -- they are fetched from the PDB by scripts/fetch_structure_metadata.py and read from structure_metadata.json. The construct's residue SPAN is NOT set here either -- it is derived from construct_scope.json (written by prepare_target.py --scope-out). Remove any optional key you don't have; the builder handles missing keys gracefully. Delete the _comment/_* keys before use (they are ignored anyway).
_domain_label_help: Optional biological NAME of the targeted domain (e.g. 'catalytic domain', 'IgV domain'). NAME ONLY -- do NOT put a residue range here. The residue span is derived from construct_scope.json and shown alongside this label, e.g. 'nominal IgV domain core 18-127; the built construct spans 17-137 after a 10 A spatial margin'.
_structure_metadata_help: Path to the structure_metadata.json sidecar written by scripts/fetch_structure_metadata.py --pdb <ID>. It carries fetched resolution/experimental method/deposition date plus a provenance block (source URL + fetch timestamp). REQUIRED whenever target_pdb is set: build_report.py fails if a PDB is named but no fetched metadata is supplied, and it never falls back to a typed value. If the fetch failed, the sidecar records available:false and the report prints 'unavailable'. Can also be passed via --structure-metadata.
_construct_scope_help: Path to the construct_scope.json sidecar written by prepare_target.py --scope-out. It is the SINGLE SOURCE of the construct span (target_range) and of the crop parameters (core_range, margin, margin_mode) used to explain nominal-vs-realised. build_report.py derives the reported range from here and cross-checks it against target_range on the metrics records; a mismatch fails the build. Can also be passed via --construct-scope.
rationale: One to three sentences on why this target matters and why a de novo mini-binder is a sensible modality (validated target, need for a small stable scaffold, etc.).
epitope_note: Optional: one or two sentences describing the region targeted and how the epitope was chosen (hotspot-guided vs unrestrained), plus any functional sites tracked.
_counts_help: Campaign counts (n_backbones, n_sequences, n_passed, n_validated) are now OPTIONAL cross-checks. They are derived by build_report.py from --all-sequences-csv, --selected-csv, and the ranking CSV. Leaving them out is the RECOMMENDED default. If you do include any of them, a value that disagrees with the derived one FAILS the build (consistency gate). Do not hand-type stale values from a previous run.
_hotspots_help: Declared epitope hotspot residue numbers (native numbering). The same set passed to prepare_target.py --hotspots, analyze_interface.py --hotspots, and ppi.hotspot_res. Cross-checked by build_report.py against hotspots_declared on the metrics records. Point this at the construct_scope.json sidecar from prepare_target.py to stay consistent. Leave empty [] if no hotspots were declared (epitope_status will be NOT_ASSESSED for all candidates).
_functional_site_help: Optional: functional/blocking-site residue numbers (e.g. a receptor-binding epitope) to check overlap against. The same set passed to analyze_interface.py --functional-site. Leave empty [] if not applicable.
_correlation_note_help: Leave empty to auto-compute from the ranking CSV with the sign-consistent convention (raw Spearman(mpnn_score, ipTM); negative = metrics agree). Only set this if you want to override the wording.
